To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the association between conflict and commitment depends on one's beliefs about the growth potential of relationships.

(1) conflict is associated with lower commitment, but (2) this association is less strong when individuals believe that relationships can grow and change, especially when they are in negative relationship circumstances (e.g., when they have a less favorable view or the problem is unresolved).
the link between experienced conflict and lower commitment is moderated by the individual's implicit theory of relationships.

the ways in which people's theories about relationships influence the ways in which conflict affects relationship commitment.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relationship between experienced conflict and relationship commitment depends on the individual's implicit theory of relationships.
the association between relationship conflict and commitment is moderated by the extent to which individuals believe relationships are capable of growing and improving over time.
growth belief moderates the relationship between conflict and commitment in a manner that is contingent on the specific circumstances of the conflict.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the benefits of conflict depend on the nature of the conflict itself.
commitment is more likely to be maintained or enhanced under negative relationship conditions when individuals believe their relationship has the potential to improve.
the benefits of growth beliefs are most pronounced under conditions of conflict and uncertainty, and that growth beliefs are most important when the relationship is in jeopardy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
people who have a growth belief about relationships are more likely to maintain their commitment to a relationship when they experience conflict.
people with growth belief are less likely to be deterred by conflict and may even benefit from conflict in the form of increased commitment.
growth belief is not always beneficial and may be most helpful under negative conditions.
